subject: Dedicated capacity follow-up — throughput targets & token economics
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@aventis.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@aventis.ai, Jules Tran <jules.tran@aventis.ai>
Date: 2027-04-18T09:04:00-07:00
Subject: Quick follow-up after today's demo — capacity questions

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for the demo this morning — the latency numbers looked promising. A few follow-ups from our side as we start to shape the procurement ask:

- Expected steady-state usage: roughly 80M tokens/day (user prompts + gen), with peaks up to ~180M tokens/day during business hours.
- Model family: we'll be running a mix of instruction-tuned models (2–7B) and a smaller set of 13B for higher-quality outputs.
- Throughput target: need to support ~120 concurrent rps at 512 tokens average generation length around peak.
- GPU preference: our infra team prefers H100 but budget may push us toward A100 80GB — need unit economics per variant.
- Budget: preliminary internal target is $2k–$6k per 1M tokens (we know this is broad — want your pricing guidance).

Can you confirm what Reserved/Dedicated SKUs you recommend (GPU type + reserved lane size) and an initial $/1M-token range for each? I'm attaching a usage snapshot for context.

Also: procurement timeline is end of May for an initial pilot.

Appreciate it —
Samir

[attachment: aventis_usage_snapshot_20270418.csv]

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@aventis.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-18T11:32:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Quick follow-up after today's demo — capacity questions

Hi Samir — great to chat earlier. Putting a concise post-demo recap here and next steps so procurement/tech can move fast. Copying Ben (pricing) and Marissa (pilot ops).

Summary of your ask (confirmed):
- Steady-state ~80M tokens/day, peak ~180M/day; avg generation length ~512 tokens; ~120 concurrent rps at peak.
- Model mix: mainly 2–7B instruction models, occasional 13B for edge cases.
- Preference: H100 ideal; A100 possible if constrained.
- Procurement target: pilot by end of May.

Initial qualification/questions we still have:
1) Token definition: do your 80M/day estimates include both prompt + generated tokens? (Your CSV helped but want to confirm allocation.)
2) SLA tolerance: is 99.9% uptime acceptable? Any hard latency SLO under 200ms for short prompts?
3) Data residency/compliance: any specific region restrictions beyond US?

Preliminary sizing guidance (high level):
- Pilot SKU (conservative): 4x H100s (shared across pinned model variants) — estimated sustained throughput ~120M tokens/day with headroom for peaks; good for validating latency/ops.
- Scale SKU (production): 8x H100s or 12x A100 80GB (cost tradeoff) — supports consistent 180M+ tokens/day with autoscale buffer.

Next steps (timeline):
- Ben to follow with costed $/1M-token bands for H100 vs A100 (three tier options: pilot, scale-min, scale-high).
- We'll produce a short 1‑page proposal + reserved SKU mapping by 4/19.
- Align on pilot start date and procurement contacts (Samir, Jules, procurement@aventis.ai).

I've attached our draft pricing worksheet (RDW_dedicated_pricing_v1.pdf) — Ben, take it away on numbers.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0187

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir@aventis.ai>, Jules Tran <jules.tran@aventis.ai>
Date: 2027-04-19T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Quick follow-up after today's demo — capacity questions

Thanks Vanessa — ran the numbers off the usage snapshot. High-level unit economics and recommended SKUs below (rounded). These are targeted for reserved/dedicated lanes with canary fallbacks to a cheaper instance pool if needed.

Token pricing assumptions (baseline):
- H100 family (dense float): lower latency, higher throughput — conservative cost basis.
- A100 80GB: lower unit capex but requires more instances for same peak throughput.

Proposed pricing bands (per 1M tokens, USD):
- Pilot (4x H100 reserved): $4,200 / 1M tokens — supports ~120M tokens/day sustained with 20% headroom. Estimated monthly committed tokens ~3.6B.
- Mid (8x H100 reserved): $3,100 / 1M tokens — supports ~220M tokens/day; monthly commit ~6.6B.
- Cost-savvy (12x A100 80GB reserved): $2,400 / 1M tokens — supports ~200M tokens/day but with slightly higher tail latency on heavy prompts; monthly commit ~6.0B.

Notes/assumptions: average generation length assumed 512 tokens; prompt tokens included in counts. These bands include infrastructure, orchestration, support, and a managed buffer. We can refine if Aventis wants a strict $/1M target — price moves materially with contract length and committed volume.

Quick suggestions for the proposal:
- Offer a 3-month pilot at the Pilot band to validate perf, then transition to Mid or Cost-savvy depending on latency tolerance.
- Include an ops-runbook and a single planned rollback to A100 pool for heavy tails.

I'll attach a short CSV with modeled throughput per SKU and a sketch of the three formal options for the 1-page proposal. Vanessa, if this looks right I'll convert into a tidy proposal and pricing page for Samir.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Director, Solutions Pricing
ben@redwood.com

Also attaching our internal budget slide to help you shape the pilot ask. If possible, can we schedule a technical deep dive next week (Thu 04/22 or Fri 04/23) to align ops and confirm model pinning strategy?

If those slots work for you, Vanessa please confirm and loop in your infra lead if needed.
